Universal meaning (locked): Explains the foundational concepts and common approaches correctly.
Key assessor question: Can they explain it accurately in their own words?
What it means when AI is used: Explains the concepts in their own words, without AI.
Minimum evidence: Proctored concept test or short viva
Typical assessment types: A01 Knowledge / Concept Assessment; A10 Structured Interview
Not this level if: Recites definitions but cannot explain or apply them to a simple example
Common misreading to avoid: Knowing about a skill is not doing it. For behavioural competencies (C04-C06), CRL 1 is not used for decisions

Universal meaning (locked): Completes familiar, well-defined tasks using known methods. Seeks guidance when conditions change or become unclear.
Key assessor question: Can they do a task like one they have practised?
What it means when AI is used: Uses tools, including AI, to complete familiar tasks, and notices when the output does not fit.
Minimum evidence: Proctored structured tasks similar to ones already practised
Typical assessment types: A02 Practical / Hands-on Task; A04 Coding / Technical Task
Not this level if: Needs step-by-step hints, or succeeds only by copying a worked solution
Common misreading to avoid: Completing a task that closely matches practice is not solving a new problem

Universal meaning (locked): Solves unfamiliar or unclear problems within a defined scope, choosing and justifying a suitable approach. May ask for information or escalate, but is not guided to the solution.
Key assessor question: Can they solve a problem they have not seen before, without being guided to the answer?
Independence: Problem level: works alone on single problems
What it means when AI is used: Frames the problem, directs AI where useful and checks the result. If they cannot explain why the solution works, it is not CRL 3, however good the output is.
Minimum evidence: Proctored, timed, unseen problems solved alone
Typical assessment types: A03 Case Study; A04 Coding / Technical Task; A05 Debugging / Troubleshooting Task; A08 Simulation
Not this level if: Needed hints toward the approach; passes obvious cases but fails edge cases; cannot explain the reasoning
Common misreading to avoid: Asking for missing information or escalating is allowed; being guided to the solution is not

Universal meaning (locked): Owns a defined piece of work from brief to usable outcome. Produces a complete, quality-checked deliverable and justifies its decisions and trade-offs.
Key assessor question: Can they produce a finished, usable piece of work and justify their choices?
Independence: Deliverable level: owns a complete piece of work
What it means when AI is used: Is accountable for every part of the deliverable, including what AI produced. Can show what they accepted, rejected and corrected, and why.
Minimum evidence: A complete deliverable plus a live defence, including a small change made on the spot
Typical assessment types: A06 Project / Take-home Assignment + A07 Live Defence / Walkthrough; A11 Presentation
Not this level if: Part of the brief is missing; cannot explain parts of their own work; cannot make the live change
Common misreading to avoid: A polished submission alone is not CRL 4. It must be defended and changed live without AI help

Universal meaning (locked): Performs a representative set of the role's responsibilities for this competency, meeting its quality standards and handling real constraints, priorities and escalation.
Key assessor question: Could they do this part of the job after normal onboarding?
Independence: Role level: handles real responsibilities over time
What it means when AI is used: Uses the team's AI tools within its rules and quality standards, in real work, over time.
Minimum evidence: Realistic role work over time, reviewed by an expert or supervisor
Typical assessment types: A12 Multi-day Work Simulation; A13 Real Work / Internship Evidence
Not this level if: Work needs major rework in review; blockers hidden until deadlines; only works on fresh, isolated tasks
Common misreading to avoid: CRL 5 is not 'expert' or 'best'. It means the level this specific role needs, and a CRL 5 for one role is not equal to CRL 5 for a more senior role

Level name: Each level includes the ones below it.
A CRL is given for one competency in one named role, never for a person overall.
CRL levels are ranks, not marks: never averaged, added or turned into percentages.
If there is not enough evidence to rate, the result is Not Rated, not CRL 0.
Partial evidence for a level means the level below.
Every rating records evidence confidence: High (live or proctored), Medium (unsupervised work defended live), Low (not usable for decisions).
